x: Coming to the scratch race, this was won by Vic Blowfield with Dick Towndrow second and Ted Stimpson third. To beat the half-hour over our course is quite good running, so it can be seen that Vic put in some really fast running, which should gain him many honours before the season is over.
Gosney of Eastleigh beat Olney the local "crack" in the individual race, but our lads packed well with Tom Clinton 4th, Dick Towndrow 5th, Ted Stimpson 6th and Frank Abberton 7th.

Dick Towndrow gained his first club championship award in being third, with a past-holder in Arthur Penny fourth, and Tom Clinton fifth. The next two positions were filled by two junior members in Martin Williamson and Mike Heard.

Dick Towndrow won the 15 miles road race promoted by the Wigmore Harriers, and Geoff Pearson and Con Abberton finished equal fifth. In the Finchley "20" Geoff Pearson was 17th in 2 hrs. 13 mins. 31 secs., quite a creditable effort.

With the help of Dick Towndrow, and such as Archie Bedford, Eddie Short, Mike Heard, “Ginger” Kennedy and Jack Brown, to mention only a few of our promising members plus the help of last season's stalwarts, I think we shall have yet another successful year over the country.

Christmas greetings were received from the undermentioned:—Borlase Hendry (Iraq); Norman and Lilian Shrubb (Trinidad and Tobago); Bill Ashford (Iran); Charlie and Doris Smart (Germany); Albert Boddy; Stan Horton; Rodney Stone; Clarice and Bill Merryman; Fred Clay; Dick Towndrow; Rene Howell; Mr. and Mrs.

Dick Towndrow and George Chantler both retired and this left our "A" team with only two finishers. George Isaacs and Gordon Doubleday also "packed up" and there were actually 141 starters but only 120 finished the course.
In a 10 miles road race which started and finished on the track, our team of Steve Charlton, Tom Carter, Dick Towndrow and Roy Minahan came second in the team race which was won by the local club.
At Reading on July 22nd our first man home was Syd Ring, who finished 28th. Dick Towndrow, Dick Tobin and George Chantler did not finish the course and our actual finishers and times were as under:—

…of our winning "National" team in 1946, is also showing signs of his old-time form, and we wish that Frank Abberton and Dick Towndrow could also strike their form of a few seasons ago in order to make up for the loss of our track "stars," who have decided not to do any serious racing over the countr…

McDonald 41, Dick Towndrow 54 and Arthur Penstone 62nd. In the Surrey 20 miles road race on May 5th, held in Richmond Park, Arthur Whitehead was our first man home in 9th place with Tom Carter 11, Syd Ring 15, Bert Jordan 19.

One way of getting your name into the Club's minutes is to change your address and one change recently notified was Dick Towndrow who has moved from one address in Mere, Wiltshire, to another in that delightful village.
